keeper_ch1_01.speaker: narrator
keeper_ch1_01.text: Below the sanctuary, there is a library. Not a room with books -- a world built of them. Shelves that curve like ribs, holding volumes in languages you've never seen.

keeper_ch1_02.speaker: narrator
keeper_ch1_02.text: The air tastes like old ink and lavender. Somewhere deep inside, a clock ticks -- slow, patient, keeping time with something that isn't hours.

keeper_ch1_03.speaker: narrator
keeper_ch1_03.text: Between the shelves, someone moves. Quick, careful hands shelving books that seem to rearrange themselves when you look away.

keeper_ch1_04.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_04.text: Oh! A visitor. I heard there was someone new. Hold on -- don't touch that shelf, it's in a mood today.

keeper_ch1_05.speaker: narrator
keeper_ch1_05.text: They emerge from between the stacks. Small, quick-eyed, with ink-stained fingers and a smile that's warm but distracted -- like they're always halfway inside a thought.

keeper_ch1_06.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_06.text: I'm the Keeper. Of stories, mostly. But also of... well, everything people forget. Or choose to forget. Or need someone to remember for them.

keeper_ch1_stories_01.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_stories_01.text: All kinds! Beginnings, endings, the mushy middles where nothing seems to happen but everything changes. Those are my favorites, actually -- the middles.

keeper_ch1_stories_02.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_stories_02.text: Everyone wants the dramatic moments. The breakthroughs. But healing? Healing happens in the quiet parts, when you're not looking.

keeper_ch1_forget_01.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_forget_01.text: Sometimes. Not on purpose. But the mind is a funny thing -- it protects you by hiding things. The problem is, it doesn't always hide the right things.

keeper_ch1_forget_02.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_forget_02.text: So I keep them. In the books, in the shelves. Safe. Until someone's ready to look at them again.

keeper_ch1_mine_01.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_mine_01.text: {keeper} stops mid-step. Looks at you with eyes that are suddenly very old, very deep.

keeper_ch1_mine_02.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_mine_02.text: I have... pieces. Fragments. Like a book someone started writing but kept putting down. There are chapters missing. Whole sections that are just blank pages.

keeper_ch1_mine_03.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_mine_03.text: But the book isn't finished, {name}. That's the important thing. The pen is still in your hand.

keeper_ch1_skill_01.speaker: narrator
keeper_ch1_skill_01.text:
[Skill Unlocked: Narrative Reframing]
You are both the author and the character of your own story. The events that happened to you are facts, but the meaning you give them is yours to shape. Asking 'What story am I telling myself about this?' can reveal narratives that no longer serve you -- and open space for new ones.

keeper_ch1_lonely_01.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_lonely_01.text: {keeper} blinks. Sets down the book they were holding. Sits on a nearby stack of encyclopedias.

keeper_ch1_lonely_02.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_lonely_02.text: It is. It really is. Everyone comes here to find something, and I help them find it, and then they leave. And I stay, with all the stories that aren't mine.

keeper_ch1_lonely_03.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_lonely_03.text: I don't usually say that out loud. You have a way of making people honest, {name}. That's either a gift or a very inconvenient superpower.

keeper_ch1_converge_01.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_converge_01.text: Come, let me show you something. There's a section of the library I think you'll like.

keeper_ch1_converge_02.speaker: narrator
keeper_ch1_converge_02.text: {keeper} leads you deeper in. The shelves narrow, then open into a small clearing. In the center: a round table, a single candle, and a book with no title on the cover.

keeper_ch1_converge_03.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_converge_03.text: This is the Memory Table. You put your hand on the book, and it shows you something. Not the future -- a memory. One that matters. One you need to see again.

keeper_ch1_converge_04.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_converge_04.text: You don't have to. But if you want... I'll be right here. Whatever comes up, you won't face it alone.

choices.text: Have you ever used it? On yourself?

keeper_ch1_memory_01.speaker: narrator
keeper_ch1_memory_01.text: You touch the book. The leather is warm, like it's been sitting in sunlight. The candle flickers.

keeper_ch1_memory_02.speaker: narrator
keeper_ch1_memory_02.text: A flash. Not a vision -- a feeling. The sensation of being small, and safe, and held. A voice humming something you can't name but your body remembers.

keeper_ch1_memory_03.speaker: narrator
keeper_ch1_memory_03.text: It lasts only a moment. When it fades, there are tears on your face. Not sad tears. The other kind -- the kind that come when something true breaks through.

keeper_ch1_memory_04.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_memory_04.text: {keeper} says nothing. They just offer you a handkerchief -- old, embroidered with tiny stars. They wait.

keeper_ch1_skill_02.speaker: narrator
keeper_ch1_skill_02.text:
[Skill Unlocked: Allowing Emotional Release]
Crying is not weakness. It's your nervous system doing exactly what it's designed to do: release tension. Tears contain stress hormones that your body is literally flushing out. Next time you feel tears coming, try letting them happen instead of holding back. Set a timer for 5 minutes if you need -- give yourself permission.

keeper_ch1_wait_01.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_wait_01.text: Good. That's good, actually. Knowing you're not ready is its own kind of wisdom. Most people dive in before they've learned to swim.

keeper_ch1_wait_02.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_wait_02.text: The book will be here. It doesn't go anywhere. Neither do I.

keeper_ch1_skill_03.speaker: narrator
keeper_ch1_skill_03.text:
[Skill Unlocked: Therapeutic Pacing]
Healing isn't a race. Going too fast can re-traumatize rather than heal. 'Not yet' is a complete answer. Trust your own timing -- your mind knows when it's safe enough to process difficult material. Pushing through isn't always brave; sometimes holding back is the braver choice.

keeper_ch1_keeper_memory_01.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_keeper_memory_01.text: {keeper} goes very still. Their hand drifts to the edge of the book but doesn't touch it.

keeper_ch1_keeper_memory_02.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_keeper_memory_02.text: Once. Just once. I saw... I saw the moment I became the Keeper. The moment I lost the person I was before.

keeper_ch1_keeper_memory_03.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_keeper_memory_03.text: I don't regret it. But I grieve it. You can do both, it turns out. Grieve something and be grateful for it at the same time.

keeper_ch1_evening_01.speaker: narrator
keeper_ch1_evening_01.text: Time moves differently in the library. When you finally look up, the candles have burned low and the shadows have grown long.

keeper_ch1_evening_02.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_evening_02.text: Come back tomorrow. I'll have tea. Real tea, not the experimental stuff the Oracle brews -- last time I'm fairly sure there was a mushroom in it that changed colors.

keeper_ch1_evening_03.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_evening_03.text: And {name}? Thank you for coming down here. Most people don't bother with the library.

choices.text: It's the best room in this place.
I think we're going to be good friends.
I'd like to help you. With the books, with the stories. If you'll let me.

keeper_ch1_end_best.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_end_best.text: {keeper} beams. It transforms their whole face -- all the worry lines vanish and what's left is pure, uncomplicated delight.

keeper_ch1_end_friends.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_end_friends.text: {keeper} laughs. Not a polite laugh -- a real one, unexpected and slightly too loud for a library.

keeper_ch1_end_friends_02.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_end_friends_02.text: Friends. Yes. I'd like that. I'd like that very much. The books are wonderful company, but they never laugh at my jokes.

keeper_ch1_end_help.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_end_help.text: {keeper} stares at you. Opens their mouth. Closes it. A book falls off a nearby shelf -- even the library seems surprised.

keeper_ch1_end_help_02.speaker: keeper
keeper_ch1_end_help_02.text: Nobody's ever asked me that before. I -- yes. Yes, I'd like that. There's so much to do, and I've been doing it alone for so long, I forgot that was a choice and not a sentence.

keeper_ch1_end_shared.speaker: narrator
keeper_ch1_end_shared.text: You leave the library carrying the smell of old books and lavender. The stairs lead you back to the main sanctuary, where a fire is burning and the evening has settled in like a cat in a sunbeam.

keeper_ch1_end_final.speaker: narrator
keeper_ch1_end_final.text: In your pocket, the deck shifts. A card slides to the edge, as if trying to show itself. You tuck it back in gently. Tomorrow. There's time.
